```python
# conformance: ignore[P028] intentional: <why this is deliberate here>
```

## P028 — `ManualQualifiedNameFString` {#p028}

**Tier:** `warn` · **Scope:** `app` · **Category:** `asset-modeling` · **Autofixable:** — · **Since:** 0.9.0

> Asset qualifiedName composed by hand with an f-string at a call site instead of one central helper

**Rationale:** qualifiedName is the identity primitive for every Atlan asset (dedup, lineage, linking).
Building it with an f-string at each call site scatters the grammar (segments, order,
separator) across the app, so an identity and the references to it can drift apart and
lineage points at an asset that does not exist. One helper per name shape keeps a single
source of truth; where a pyatlan asset .creator() produces the identical string, the
helper derives it from the creator, which also rejects blank segments.

### What correct looks like

- **Compliant example:** atlan-openapi-app app/asset_mapper.py — qualifiedName comes from `APISpec.creator()` /
  `APIPath.creator()`, so the grammar is pyatlan's. Where a caller needs the string and
  not the asset, atlan-metabase-app app/qualified_names.py keeps one memoized helper per
  name shape that returns the creator's `.qualified_name`, and one per process shape.
- **Migrate with:** the `migrate-asset-modeling` skill (`skills-dir`)
- **Already correct when:** A justified per-function inline `# conformance: ignore[P028] <reason>` IS the correct
  end state in three cases, and the reason must say which. Either no pyatlan creator
  produces the identical string for every input the app can receive (an asset family
  without creators, a content-hashed ARS key, or a creator that derives a segment
  differently or raises on a reachable blank input), in which case the reason names the
  creator or says none exists, and the f-string lives in one helper per name shape (by
  convention in app/qualified_names.py; the detector does not check the location) rather
  than being repeated. Or the f-string is a Process / ColumnProcess / BIProcess identity
  in one helper per process shape: `generate_qualified_name(process_id=...)` only
  prefixes the connection and needs placeholder inputs, so a helper that calls it and a
  helper that keeps the f-string with a reason naming it are both accepted when they
  produce the qualifiedName the app emits today. Or the f-string is not an identity at
  all (an object-store key or prefix starting with the qn, a trailing-`/` match prefix,
  a log/exception message or display text), and the reason names what the string is. A
  directive on a non-process identity site whose creator produces the identical string
  for every reachable input is unremediated: that helper returns the creator's
  `.qualified_name`.

An f-string composes a slash-delimited `qualifiedName` — it both interpolates a
`*qualified_name` / `*_qn` value and contains a `/` separator (e.g.
`f"{connection_qualified_name}/{schema}"`). qualifiedName is Atlan's asset identity;
hand-building it at each call site repeats the grammar across the app, so an identity
and the references to it can drift apart with no single source of truth.

Not flagged — object-store keys: a qn reference preceded by a `/`-bearing literal
segment (e.g. `f"persistent-artifacts/.../{connection_qualified_name}/publish-state"`)
is a storage path that embeds a qn, not an asset qualifiedName rooted at its parent qn,
so it is not flagged.

Fix: keep each qualifiedName grammar in one helper per name shape and call the helpers
from every site (by convention all in `app/qualified_names.py`; the detector does not
check the location). A helper returns `X.creator(...).qualified_name` when that creator
produces the identical string for every input the app can receive; otherwise it keeps
the f-string with `# conformance: ignore[P028] <reason>`.  A Process / ColumnProcess /
BIProcess helper may do either: `generate_qualified_name` with `process_id` only
prefixes the connection, needs placeholder inputs, and returns a hash instead when
`process_id` is blank, so both shapes are accepted when they produce the qualifiedName
the app emits today.  A `process_id` f-string is itself flagged only when it
interpolates a qualifiedName and contains a `/` literal (`f"{model_qn}@allmodule"` is
not flagged); a flagged one takes the same ignore.

Not an identity — suppress with a reason: an f-string that embeds a qualifiedName but
does not build an asset identity is a false positive of this name-and-`/` heuristic.
This covers an object-store key or prefix that *starts* with the qn (e.g.
`f"{connection_qn}/lineage_current_state"`), a trailing-`/` match `prefix` (`f"{qn}/"`
used with `startswith`), and a log or exception message or display text.  Suppress it
with `# conformance: ignore[P028] <reason>`, where the reason names what the string is
(for example `object-store key, not a qualifiedName`). Do not rewrite it through a
creator.
